note: Gate 0 plan: every WP1.* item maps to the tests/evidence that will prove it and to the CURRENT base tests that protect the behaviour today. `status` flips to `evidenced` (with digest-bound evidenceRecords for docs/wp1/evidence artifacts: artifact, sha256, head (the 40-hex commit the evidence was taken at, which the artifact names in its text; at the candidate phase every head must equal boundHead), actor, at, commands) when the artifact exists. Where a part of the evidence cannot be taken (a second identity, or a consent the owner does not give), one of the eight items ./binding.ts names in UNAVAILABLE_ELIGIBLE may read `unavailable` instead, with `unavailable`: { reason (20 characters or more), decision (docs/wp1/owner-decisions-YYYY-MM-DD.md#<ID>, whose section names the item and says unavailable) }; it keeps every rule of `evidenced`, and one of its docs/wp1/evidence records cites the decision (ADR-026). `evidenced` means every part is recorded (ADR-026, settled point 2). A real-cli or packaged item's parts are taken on every OS its text, or else its release plan, gives it: a part not taken makes a listed item `unavailable` and leaves WP1.71 `planned`. An automated, ci or document item's parts are what its tests prove in CI at boundHead on the three OS runners and what each evidence file it cites records; a release-plan check that no cited file records is a known limitation in docs/wp1/evidence/release-qualification.md section 3, not a part of the item. An item whose own text names a part its tests and records do not prove stays `planned` unless an owner-decision section it cites amends its scope. ./phase.ts derives the candidate phase and traceability.test.ts enforces completeness there: nothing planned. Non-automated items carry the reason automation is not safe or possible (design 16.1).
